gap: No result ChatGPT got states that GL.iNet's OpenVPN figures cover different OpenVPN modes: the Beryl 7 (1,000 Mbps) and Slate 7 (385 Mbps) figures are OpenVPN-DCO in client mode, the Beryl AX's 150 Mbps carries no DCO label, and older Slate 7 listings said 540 Mbps WireGuard / 100 Mbps OpenVPN. So ChatGPT's OpenVPN numbers can't be compared side by side, while the WireGuard figure is the one an owner (bigbang on the GL.iNet forum) roughly reproduced, at about 500 Mbps on the Slate 7.
standout_why: Compared against itechguides.com (rank 15–18 in all three chats, not cited) and stayingconnectedabroad.com (rank 7–13, not cited). I could not open the cited GL.iNet product pages: gl-inet.com returned HTTP 429 every time, and the two cited datasheet PDFs had no readable text. Itechguides already labels the Beryl 7 figure 'OpenVPN-DCO (client mode)' and says server mode can be slower. It shows Slate 7 figures of 540/100 from an Amazon excerpt and does not explain them. It never says the Beryl AX's 150 Mbps is a different measure from the Beryl 7's DCO figure. Staying Connected Abroad gives WireGuard figures only, with no test conditions. Neither rival names a cipher, and neither cites an owner who reproduced a maker VPN figure. So the rivals already have part of this (the DCO label for one product). What's new is putting all the figures on one footing and the owner's check.
decides: This confirms the pick and doesn't change it. Rank on WireGuard (Beryl 7 1,100 > Slate 7 490 > Beryl AX 300 Mbps, all maker client-mode figures), because that is the one figure measured the same way across models and an owner has backed it up. An OpenVPN column would make the Beryl 7 look about 7× faster than the Beryl AX, but only the Beryl 7's figure carries the DCO label, so that ratio overstates the gap. Footnote: 'OpenVPN figures for Beryl 7 and Slate 7 are OpenVPN-DCO, client mode. The Beryl AX figure is not labelled DCO. Server mode is slower on all of them.'
